item.title: Reported shooting closes Eisenhower Expressway near Austin for hours
item.description: Illinois State Police closed all westbound lanes of the Eisenhower Expressway near Austin Avenue for about three hours early Friday while investigating a reported shooting. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Trump donor claims Kimberly Guilfoyle asked him to wire her $100,000 for political access
item.description: Businessman Eric Deters, a Trump donor, says U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle asked him to pay a $100,000 bill as "quid pro quo" for access to Trump administration officials.

item.title: Trump ally who claims Kimberly Guilfoyle asked for $100,000 speaks to CBS News
item.description: Trump donor and businessman Eric Deters spoke to CBS News' Weijia Jiang about his allegations involving Kimberly Guilfoyle. Deters says she asked for $100,000 to pay her American Express bill in exchange for her help with the Trump administration.

item.title: Police say a Missouri teen was killed in a hit and run. Her family has questions.
item.description: Police say Persephone Berger, 16, was struck and killed in a hit and run. Her family says police accounts of her death don't add up. Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Sen. Murphy accuses Trump administration of "cover-up" over blocked U.S. base access
item.description: Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy says he was blocked from accessing a U.S. base as part of a Trump administration "cover-up" linked to the Iran war. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has more.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias becomes Category 3 storm as it threatens northern Gulf Coast
item.description: Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, has been getting stronger as it takes aim at the Gulf Coast from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: Iran's Houthi allies step up deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Saudi Arabia says missile strikes by Iran's Houthi allies killed three people at Riyadh's airport as fighting escalates in the Middle East conflict's new epicenter.

item.title: Miranda Lambert reveals inspiration behind Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" song she co-wrote
item.description: Miranda Lambert talks to Anthony Mason about combining country and disco for her new album, "Crisco," and reveals the inspiration behind Ella Langley's record-breaking hit song "Choosin' Texas," which she co-wrote.

item.title: Protests erupt after ICE agent shoots NYC man who was in car with 5-year-old son
item.description: Oscar Belgal, 28, was shot in the neck by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in New York City, officials say. Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Turbulence injures eight on Avianca flight that was forced to divert to MIA
item.description: The Avianca flight was headed from Colombia to New York City when the turbulence forced it to divert to MIA, officials say.

item.title: Heated Senate debates in Georgia, Maine and Michigan
item.description: Senate candidates in Georgia, Maine and Michigan squared off in heated debates ahead of the midterm elections. Caitlin Huey-Burns breaks it down.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias becomes Category 3 storm
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is barreling toward the U.S. and has strengthened to a Category 3 storm. CBS News' Jason Allen and Rob Marciano report.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter's firing squad execution to be livestreamed, Pentagon says
item.description: Former U.S. Army officer Nidal Malik Hasan was convicted of shooting and killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009. Now, the U.S. military plans to execute him by firing squad and livestream it. Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: What we know about the ICE shooting in New York City
item.description: An ICE agent shot and injured a man in New York City's Bronx borough while his 5-year-old son was in the car, according to Democratic Rep. Adriano Espaillat. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Shock after news that Fort Hood shooter's execution could be livestreamed
item.description: A Pentagon official says the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army major who was convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood, will be livestreamed. CBS News' Taurean Small reports.

item.title: Jon Ossoff slams Mike Collins in Georgia debate, claims he promoted neo-Nazi content
item.description: Georgia senatorial candidates Jon Ossoff and Mike Collins engaged in a debate ahead of the midterms, where both traded attacks on the economy, tariffs, healthcare cuts, data centers and more. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Chipotle shares jump after report that Starbucks has explored a takeover
item.description: A move by Starbucks to buy the fast-casual Mexican chain would combine two of the most recognizable restaurant brands.

item.title: Mike Rogers clashes with Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan debate over Iran, Hamas and Israel
item.description: Michigan senatorial candidates Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed clashed during a debate before the midterm elections. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has some fact-checking on some of the claims made.

item.title: Eye Opener: Gulf Coast prepares for Hurricane Isaias
item.description: Mandatory evacuations are underway as Hurricane Isaias heads toward the northern Gulf Coast. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Nobel Peace Prize awarded to former ICC judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay
item.description: Nobel Peace Prize 2026 was awarded to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a former judge on the International Criminal Court, drawing a quick, angry rebuke from Israel.

item.title: Firsthand look at the high-tech hunt for cargo thieves
item.description: Cargo theft has become a multibillion-dollar business, and consumers are paying the price.

item.title: Police launch first-of-its-kind national crackdown on train cargo theft
item.description: In a first-of-its-kind national blitz shown exclusively to CBS News, federal agents, railroad police and law enforcement in more than two dozen states hit the tracks and highways on the same night, using infrared drone cameras to track down thieves targeting cargo trains.

item.title: Guilfoyle associate says when she asked him for $100K, it was "quid pro quo"
item.description: White House officials were told that text messages between Kimberly Guilfoyle and Eric Deters were real, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Judge presses Justice Department on justifications for White House media ban
item.description: Lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico were back in court as the legal battle continues over President Trump's decision to ban their reporters from the White House.

item.title: 2 Renoir paintings stolen from French museum recovered, mayor says
item.description: Two paintings by the French impressionist master Renoir stolen a month ago from a museum dedicated to the artist have been recovered, according to the local mayor.

item.title: "Hallelujah" fills the Basilica of Saint Francis | 60 Minutes
item.description: Voices ring out as the choir performs the "Hallelujah" chorus. 60 Minutes captured the music on Pentecost Sunday at the Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi in Italy.

item.title: Obama raises more than $13 million for Democrats
item.description: Former President Barack Obama, who ran on "hope and change," is resurrecting his signature campaign slogan in a new series of digital ads for the Democratic National Committee that were viewed exclusively by CBS News.

item.title: AI leaders lobby Trump health officials in government-run chat room
item.description: A Slack workspace has served as a war room for AI industry insiders and Trump administration officials to launch a rapid campaign aimed at persuading Americans to manage their healthcare and medical records on apps.

item.title: Creators of Israeli series "Fauda" on the show's unexpected popularity in Lebanon
item.description: "Fauda," an Israeli drama series on Netflix, confronts the traumas of the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks in Israel in its fifth season. CBS News' Chris Livesay reports on the show's unexpected popularity in Lebanon.

item.title: These documents tell the story of the Cornell rape allegations
item.description: Hundreds of pages of documents obtained by CBS News detail Jane Doe's allegations, the Cornell police investigation and responses of some of the accused Chi Phi fraternity members.
